mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of >1% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated increase in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust recovery in household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both above 6-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 6-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher earnings growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when UNRATE remains below 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 4% for two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 exceeds 4% annualized for two consecutive quarters.
